subject: DPA: subprocessor delegation, dataflow retention matrix & UK IDTA sequencing
messages:
From: Evelyn Carter <evelyn.carter@lumenhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-27T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: DPA: subprocessor delegation & retention mapping for LumenHealth

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

Thanks for the earlier call. As we start our DPA review for the upcoming renewal, Legal & Security need a consolidated view of Redwood's subprocessors and a retention matrix that maps data categories to retention periods and routing controls (SCC/UK IDTA/TIA distinctions). Specifically can you confirm the following: 

- Canonical list of subcontractors that process customer content (name, primary jurisdiction, role)
- For each: whether they process data in EU, UK, US, or APAC and whether any offshoring exceptions exist
- Retention buckets by data type (PII, logs, telemetry, KV cache snapshots) and whether retention is configurable per-customer
- Which safeguards apply per flow: SCCs, UK IDTA / UK Addendum, or an accepted TIA/DTIA
- Evidence we can put on our tracker: SOC2, subprocessor contracts (clauses calling out cross-border), and a statement on key custody (KMS/HSM usage)

Can you provide an initial matrix and a target deadline? Procurement will need this to complete our supplier risk assessment and confirm routing for EU patients.

Attachments requested: a basic CSV template where we can map the fields above.

Best,
Evelyn Carter
Head of Vendor Security | LumenHealth
E: evelyn.carter@lumenhealth.com
A: LumenHealth, 4th Floor, 120 Fleet St.

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Carter <evelyn.carter@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-28T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: subprocessor delegation & retention mapping for LumenHealth

Evelyn — thanks for the clear list. We're happy to own this and propose the following approach so Legal & Security can consume the artifacts in a predictable way:

Plan (proposed):
1) We attach an initial "subprocessor + routing matrix" (xlsx) that lists current subprocessors, primary processing jurisdiction, and default routing.
2) We add a retention matrix tab that maps: PII (customer content), logs (request, inferencing, audit), KV cache snapshots, and metrics -> to default retention periods and whether the value is adjustable per-customer.
3) We provide supporting evidence: latest SOC2 report (Q1 2028), redlined subprocessor clause excerpts, and a statement on KMS usage (Redwood uses customer-provided or managed KMS for Private deployments; hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS, keys in HSM-backed provider).
4) For routing/safeguards: we indicate where SCCs apply, where the UK IDTA/UK Addendum is bound by contract, and when we recommend a TIA. We'll flag flows that require explicit DTIA/TIA execution.

Timeline: initial package by EOD 2028-06-30; follow-up with additional artifacts (signed subprocessor clauses) by 2028-07-07 if needed. If that timeline works, we'll schedule a 30-minute walkthrough next week to walk Security through the matrix.

Note on subprocessors: the matrix will call out the two primary infra subprocessors (CloudOpsCo — US; LogVault — EU-managed cluster), our metrics provider (TelemetryInc — US), and a smaller CDN partner (edge infra — APAC + EU POA). We'll also mark whether any subcontractor processes customer content (no for metrics; yes for storage & inference routing).

I attached the initial matrix and the SOC2 stub. If Procurement wants legal redlines, we can push the current DPA v3 draft to DocuSign once redlines are resolved.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Privacy | Redwood Inference
Attachment: redwood_subprocessor_matrix_20280628.xlsx (xlsx)
Attachment: redwood_soc2_report_q1_2028.pdf (pdf)

---
From: LumenHealth Procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Carter <evelyn.carter@lumenhealth.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-29T10:05:00+01:00
Subject: Re: DPA: subprocessor delegation & retention mapping for LumenHealth

Kimberly — thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few clarifications Procurement needs before we can move the DPA to our legal queue: 

- Retention: can you confirm the default retention windows in days for request logs, inference logs, and KV cache snapshots? We have a strict 90-day max for certain patient-identifiable telemetry.
- Onshore/offshore handling: you mentioned LogVault has an EU-managed cluster — is that contractualized as an EU-only processing subprocessor for LumenHealth customers, or does it fail open to US for disaster recovery?
- Key custody: we need explicit confirmation that for Private deployments LumenHealth can bring its own KMS and that keys do not leave customer control. A short proof point or link to the integration guide is helpful.
- Also please flag any subprocessors that are not covered by SCCs/UK IDTA and would require a TIA/DTIA.

If you can surface those three datapoints in the matrix (simple columns), Procurement can complete the risk assessment and push it to Legal later this week.

Procurement (on behalf of LumenHealth)
procurement@lumenhealth.com

---
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Carter <evelyn.carter@lumenhealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-01T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA: subprocessor delegation & retention mapping for LumenHealth

Team — quick update and deliverables per Procurement asks. See attachments and notes below.

Deliverables attached (updated 2028-07-01):
- redwood_subprocessor_matrix_20280628.xlsx (updated) -> now contains columns: DefaultRetentionDays, EUOnlyProcessingFlag, NeedsTIAFlag.
- redwood_soc2_report_q1_2028.pdf (unchanged)
- dpa_draft_lumen_v3.docx -> current DPA draft with Redwood comments (high level redlines)

Quick answers inline: 
- Retention defaults: Request logs = 180 days, Inference logs = 90 days (configurable down to 30 for enterprise plans), KV cache snapshots = 7 days by default (can be disabled for Private deployments).
- LogVault EU cluster: contractualized as EU-only for customers that sign the UK IDTA / EU-specific routing addendum. Disaster recovery to US is only used for emergency DR and requires explicit customer opt-in; we flag it in the matrix (EUOnlyProcessingFlag = true for LumenHealth by default).
- KMS: Private deployments support customer-managed KMS with HSM-backed key stores (we have an integration guide here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c4d5e). For hosted customers we use Redwood-managed KMS; keys are in HSM-managed provider but not customer-controlled unless a Private deployment is purchased.
- TIA flags: two subprocessors (TelemetryInc and EdgeCDN Co) are flagged NeedsTIA = true because they operate global-edge networks not covered by SCC/IDTA in default configuration; we propose either (a) routing policy to avoid these subprocessors for LumenHealth EU traffic, or (b) execute a TIA for those flows.

Next steps:
- If Procurement confirms this matrix satisfies the tracker, Legal can pick up dpa_draft_lumen_v3.docx for redlines.
- If LumenHealth prefers routing-only mitigations (avoid TelemetryInc/EdgeCDN for EU patient traffic), we'll raise an internal route policy and update the matrix with a policy ID.

I'll be on the walkthrough on Wednesday — Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Privacy | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
